flavor.black: They can live both in the ocean and on land. A slap from one of them is enough to open a hole in the bottom of a tanker.
flavor.white: Incredible jaw strength enables them to chew up steel beams and rocks along with their prey.

flavor.black: Said to be an ancestor of bird Pokémon, they were unable to fly and moved about by hopping from one branch to another.
flavor.white: Revived from a fossil, this Pokémon is thought to be the ancestor of all bird Pokémon.

flavor.black: They are intelligent and will cooperate to catch prey. From the ground, they use a running start to take flight.
flavor.white: It runs better than it flies. It catches prey by running at speeds comparable to those of an automobile.

flavor.black: Inhaling the gas they belch will make you sleep for a week. They prefer unsanitary places.
flavor.white: The combination of garbage bags and industrial waste caused the chemical reaction that created this Pokémon.

flavor.black: It clenches opponents with its left arm and finishes them off with foul-smelling poison gas belched from its mouth.
flavor.white: They absorb garbage and make it part of their bodies. They shoot a poisonous liquid from their right-hand fingertips.

flavor.black: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.
flavor.white: To protect themselves from danger, they hide their true identities by transforming into people and Pokémon.

flavor.black: Bonds between these Pokémon are very strong. It protects the safety of its pack by tricking its opponents.
flavor.white: Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.

flavor.black: They greet one another by rubbing each other with their tails, which are always kept well groomed and clean.
flavor.white: These Pokémon prefer a tidy habitat. They are always sweeping and dusting, using their tails as brooms.

flavor.black: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.
flavor.white: Their white fur feels amazing to touch. Their fur repels dust and prevents static electricity from building up.

flavor.black: Their ribbonlike feelers increase their psychic power. They are always staring at something.
flavor.white: They intently observe both Trainers and Pokémon. Apparently, they are looking at something that only Gothita can see.

flavor.black: They use hypnosis to control people and Pokémon. Tales of Gothorita leading people astray are told in every corner.
flavor.white: Starlight is the source of their power. At night, they mark star positions by using psychic power to float stones.

flavor.black: Starry skies thousands of light-years away are visible in the space distorted by their intense psychic power.
flavor.white: They can predict the future from the placement and movement of the stars. They can see Trainers’ life spans.

flavor.black: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.
flavor.white: Because their bodies are enveloped in a special liquid, they can survive in any environment.

flavor.black: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.
flavor.white: When their brains, now divided in two, are thinking the same thoughts, these Pokémon exhibit their maximum power.

flavor.black: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.
flavor.white: These remarkably intelligent Pokémon fight by controlling arms that can grip with rock-crushing power.

flavor.black: These bird Pokémon are excellent divers. They swim around in the water eating their favorite food--peat moss.
flavor.white: When attacked, it uses its feathers to splash water, escaping under cover of the spray.

flavor.black: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.
flavor.white: It administers sharp, powerful pecks with its bill. It whips its long neck to deliver forceful repeated strikes.

flavor.black: The temperature of their breath is -58° F. They create snow crystals and make snow fall in the areas around them.
flavor.white: This Pokémon formed from icicles bathed in energy from the morning sun. It sleeps buried in snow.

flavor.black: Snowy mountains are this Pokémon’s habitat. During an ancient ice age, they moved to southern areas.
flavor.white: It conceals itself from enemy eyes by creating many small ice particles and hiding among them.

flavor.black: Swallowing large amounts of water, they make snow clouds inside their bodies and attack their foes with violent blizzards.
flavor.white: If both heads get angry simultaneously, this Pokémon expels a blizzard, burying everything in snow.

flavor.black: The color and scent of their fur changes to match the mountain grass. When they sense hostility, they hide in the grass.
flavor.white: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

flavor.black: They migrate according to the seasons. People can tell the season by looking at Sawsbuck’s horns.
flavor.white: The plants growing on its horns change according to the season. The leaders of the herd possess magnificent horns.

flavor.black: The energy made in its cheeks’ electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.
flavor.white: They live on treetops and glide using the inside of a cape-like membrane while discharging electricity.

flavor.black: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.
flavor.white: When they feel threatened, they spit an acidic liquid to drive attackers away. This Pokémon targets Shelmet.

flavor.black: They fly around at high speed, striking with their pointed spears. Even when in trouble, they face opponents bravely.
flavor.white: These Pokémon evolve by wearing the shell covering of a Shelmet. The steel armor protects their whole body.

flavor.black: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.
flavor.white: For some reason, this Pokémon resembles a Poké Ball. They release poison spores to repel those who try to catch them.

flavor.black: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.
flavor.white: They show off their Poké Ball caps to lure prey, but very few Pokémon are fooled by this.

flavor.black: With its thin, veil-like arms wrapped around the body of its opponent, it sinks to the ocean floor.
flavor.white: They paralyze prey with poison, then drag them down to their lairs, five miles below the surface.

flavor.black: The fate of the ships and crew that wander into Jellicent’s habitat: all sunken, all lost, all vanished.
flavor.white: They propel themselves by expelling absorbed seawater from their bodies. Their favorite food is life energy.

flavor.black: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.
flavor.white: Floating in the open sea is how they live. When they find a wounded Pokémon, they embrace it and bring it to shore.

flavor.black: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.
flavor.white: They attach themselves to large-bodied Pokémon and absorb static electricity, which they store in an electric pouch.

flavor.black: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.
flavor.white: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

flavor.black: When threatened, it attacks by shooting a barrage of spikes, which gives it a chance to escape by rolling away.
flavor.white: They stick their spikes into cave walls and absorb the minerals they find in the rock.

flavor.black: It fights by swinging around its three spiky feelers. A hit from these steel spikes can reduce a boulder to rubble.
flavor.white: They attach themselves to cave ceilings, firing steel spikes at targets passing beneath them.

flavor.black: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.
flavor.white: Interlocking two bodies and spinning around generates the energy they need to live.

flavor.black: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.
flavor.white: Spinning minigears are rotated at high speed and repeatedly fired away. It is dangerous if the gears don’t return.

flavor.black: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.
flavor.white: The gear with the red core is rotated at high speed for a rapid energy charge.

flavor.black: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.
flavor.white: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

flavor.black: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.
flavor.white: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

flavor.black: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.
flavor.white: With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

flavor.black: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent’s brain, causing unendurable headaches.
flavor.white: This Pokémon had never been seen until it appeared from far in the desert 50 years ago.

flavor.black: It can manipulate an opponent’s memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.
flavor.white: It uses psychic power to control an opponent’s brain and tamper with its memories.

flavor.black: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.
flavor.white: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.

flavor.black: This ominous Pokémon is feared. Through cities it wanders, searching for the spirits of the fallen.
flavor.white: It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.

flavor.black: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.
flavor.white: Being consumed in Chandelure’s flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

flavor.black: They use their tusks to crush the berries they eat. Repeated regrowth makes their tusks strong and sharp.
flavor.white: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.

flavor.black: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they’ve been fighting.
flavor.white: Their tusks can shatter rocks. Territory battles between Fraxure can be intensely violent.

flavor.black: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.
flavor.white: Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.

flavor.black: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.
flavor.white: Its nose is always running. It sniffs the snot back up because the mucus provides the raw material for its moves.

flavor.black: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.
flavor.white: It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.

flavor.black: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.
flavor.white: They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

flavor.black: When attacked, it defends itself by closing the lid of its shell. It can spit a sticky, poisonous liquid.
flavor.white: It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.

flavor.black: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.
flavor.white: Having removed its heavy shell, it becomes very light and can fight with ninja-like movements.

flavor.black: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.
flavor.white: It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.

flavor.black: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.
flavor.white: They have mastered elegant combos. As they concentrate, their battle moves become swifter and more precise.

flavor.black: It wields the fur on its arms like a whip. Its arm attacks come with such rapidity that they cannot even be seen.
flavor.white: They use the long fur on their arms as a whip to strike their opponents.

flavor.black: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.
flavor.white: It races through narrow caves, using its sharp claws to catch prey. The skin on its face is harder than a rock.

flavor.black: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.
flavor.white: These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.

flavor.black: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.
flavor.white: It is said that Golurk were ordered to protect people and Pokémon by the ancient people who made them.

flavor.black: Blades comprise this Pokémon’s entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.
flavor.white: They fight at Bisharp’s command. They cling to their prey and inflict damage by sinking their blades into it.

flavor.black: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.
flavor.white: Bisharp pursues prey in the company of a large group of Pawniard. Then Bisharp finishes off the prey.

flavor.black: Their fluffy fur absorbs damage, even if they strike foes with a fierce headbutt.
flavor.white: They charge wildly and headbutt everything. Their headbutts have enough destructive force to derail a train.

flavor.black: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.
flavor.white: They will challenge anything, even strong opponents, without fear. Their frequent fights help them become stronger.

flavor.black: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.
flavor.white: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

flavor.black: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.
flavor.white: They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.

flavor.black: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.
flavor.white: Watching from the sky, they swoop to strike weakened Pokémon on the ground. They decorate themselves with bones.

flavor.black: It breathes through a hole in its tail while it burns with an internal fire. Durant is its prey.
flavor.white: Using their very hot, flame-covered tongues, they burn through Durant’s steel bodies and consume their insides.

flavor.black: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.
flavor.white: Durant dig nests in mountains. They build their complicated, interconnected tunnels into mazes.

flavor.black: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.
flavor.white: They cannot see, so they tackle and bite to learn about their surroundings. Their bodies are covered in wounds.

flavor.black: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.
flavor.white: Since their two heads do not get along and compete with each other for food, they always eat too much.

flavor.black: This brutal Pokémon travels the skies on its six wings. Anything that moves seems like a foe to it, triggering its attack.
flavor.white: The heads on their arms do not have brains. They use all three heads to consume and destroy everything.

flavor.black: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.
flavor.white: The base of volcanoes is where they make their homes. They shoot fire from their five horns to repel attacking enemies.

flavor.black: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona’s fire provided a replacement for the sun.
flavor.white: A sea of fire engulfs the surroundings of their battles, since they use their six wings to scatter their ember scales.

flavor.black: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.
flavor.white: It has a body and heart of steel. Its glare is sufficient to make even an unruly Pokémon obey it.

flavor.black: This Pokémon came to the defense of Pokémon that had lost their homes in a war among humans.
flavor.white: Its charge is strong enough to break through a giant castle wall in one blow. This Pokémon is spoken of in legends.

flavor.black: This Pokémon fought humans in order to protect its friends. Legends about it continue to be passed down.
flavor.white: Its head sprouts horns as sharp as blades. Using whirlwind-like movements, it confounds and swiftly cuts opponents.

flavor.black: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.
flavor.white: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

flavor.black: Countless charred remains mar the landscape of places through which Thundurus has passed.
flavor.white: The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

flavor.black: This Pokémon appears in legends. It sends flames into the air from its tail, burning up everything around it.
flavor.white: When Reshiram’s tail flares, the heat energy moves the atmosphere and changes the world’s weather.

flavor.black: Concealing itself in lightning clouds, it flies throughout the Unova region. It creates electricity in its tail.
flavor.white: This Pokémon appears in legends. In its tail, it has a giant generator that creates electricity.

flavor.black: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”
flavor.white: The energy that comes pouring from its tail increases the nutrition in the soil, making crops grow to great size.

flavor.black: It generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out.
flavor.white: It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

flavor.black: By blasting water from its hooves, it can glide across water. It excels at using leg moves while battling.
flavor.white: It crosses the world, running over the surfaces of oceans and rivers. It appears at scenic waterfronts.

flavor.black: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.
flavor.white: Many famous songs have been inspired by the melodies that Meloetta plays.

flavor.black: Over 300 million years ago, it was feared as the strongest of hunters. It has been modified by Team Plasma.
flavor.white: This ancient bug Pokémon was altered by Team Plasma. They upgraded the cannon on its back.
